title: CloudSEK: Silent Lynx group took Tajik government documents, including Defence Ministry mail, via railway employee account
date_note: Date of CloudSEK's report as relayed by BES.media on 12 November; the activity ran from mid-August to at least 10 October 2026.
summary: Per a Reuters report relayed by BES.media, security firm CloudSEK attributes the intrusion to the Silent Lynx group, which entered Tajikistan's government e-document system through a Tajik railway employee's account, from mid-August to at least 10 October. More than two thousand documents addressed to or passing through the Defence Ministry were taken, plus National Guard, security committee and investment committee material. CloudSEK links the group to Kazakhstan with moderate confidence; no government confirmed it.
plain: Researchers say a hacking group read Tajikistan's government document system for about two months and copied thousands of documents, including defence mail. Governments have not confirmed it.
exec: Shows how one compromised employee account at a state railway can open a government-wide document system; relevant to regional government and transport operators.
action: Government and rail operators in Central Asia: review e-document system logins since August, enforce MFA on staff accounts and check for exposure of mail routed through shared document platforms.
impact: More than two thousand documents tied to the Tajik Defence Ministry reported taken; hundreds of letters of the State Committee for Investments.

validation.note: Secondary Russian-language relay of Reuters/CloudSEK; the Kazakh and Tajik governments did not respond; Kazakhstan link is the researchers' moderate-confidence assessment, not an official attribution.

review.note: Compared title, dates (CloudSEK report 11 Nov, BES relay 12 Nov, mid-Aug to at least 10 Oct), railway account access, more than two thousand Defence Ministry documents, hundreds of investment committee letters, moderate-confidence Kazakhstan link and no government response against the BES.media page
